idiom-31-q06.truthCondition: Ben and his flatmate often argue fiercely about cleaning their shared kitchen.
idiom-31-q06.correctReason: 原題說 Ben 與同住者經常為清潔共用廚房激烈爭執；正確句保留人物、頻率及爭議內容。

foils.text: Ben and his flatmate fight like cat and dog over using their shared kitchen.
foils.reason: 這句把爭議由「清潔廚房」改成「使用廚房」，不是原題所說的事。

foils.text: Ben and his flatmate used to fight like cat and dog over cleaning their shared kitchen.
foils.reason: 「used to」暗示經常爭吵的情況已經過去；原題說他們現在仍常常爭執。

foils.text: Ben and his flatmate hardly ever fight like cat and dog over cleaning their shared kitchen.
foils.reason: 「hardly ever」表示很少爭吵，與原題的「經常」相反。

idiom-31-q07.truthCondition: The two classmates argue angrily over every small mistake, which prevents them from working together.
idiom-31-q07.correctReason: 兩名同學連小錯誤都會吵起來；正確句以慣用語交代反覆激烈的爭執。

foils.text: The two classmates never fight like cat and dog over small mistakes.
foils.reason: 「never」說兩人不會因小錯誤激烈爭吵；原題說每遇小錯誤都會吵起來。

foils.text: The two classmates fight like cat and dog over only major mistakes.
foils.reason: 「only major mistakes」把原題的「每個小錯誤」改成只為重大錯誤爭吵。

foils.text: The two classmates work calmly together despite every small mistake.
foils.reason: 這句改成兩人能平靜合作，與原題說他們無法共事相反。

idiom-31-q08.truthCondition: The speaker's parents argued angrily and often about money in the past, but are calmer now.
idiom-31-q08.correctReason: 「used to fight like cat and dog」表達父母以前常為金錢激烈爭吵，而現在已較平靜。

foils.text: My parents still fight like cat and dog about money.
foils.reason: 「still」表示現在仍經常激烈爭吵；原題說他們現在已平靜得多。

foils.text: My parents used to fight like cat and dog about school rules.
foils.reason: 這句把爭議由「金錢」改成「學校規則」，改變原題內容。

foils.text: My parents used to argue fiercely about money.
foils.reason: 這句保留舊日爭吵的事實，卻未用上本課要求的英語慣用語。

idiom-31-q09.truthCondition: Grace and Ella argued fiercely throughout the entire trip, from the first day to the last.
idiom-31-q09.correctReason: 「during the whole trip」保留從首天到最後一天都激烈爭執的時間範圍，並自然用上慣用語。

foils.text: Grace and Ella fought like cat and dog on the first day of the trip.
foils.reason: 「on the first day」只涵蓋首天；原題說爭吵一直持續至旅程最後一天。

foils.text: Grace and Mia fought like cat and dog during the whole trip.
foils.reason: 這句把爭吵的其中一人由 Ella 改成 Mia，與原題不符。

foils.text: Grace and Ella argued fiercely during the whole trip.
foils.reason: 這句保留了旅程中的爭吵，卻沒有完成使用目標慣用語的改寫。

idiom-31-q10.truthCondition: Every disagreement between the two team captains becomes an angry argument.
idiom-31-q10.correctReason: 原題說兩名隊長每次意見不同都會變成激烈爭吵；正確句保留「每次」的反覆模式。

foils.text: The two team captains never fight like cat and dog when they disagree.
foils.reason: 「never」說兩人意見不同時不會激烈爭吵；原題卻說每次意見不同都會吵起來。

foils.text: The two team captains fought like cat and dog whenever they disagreed.
foils.reason: 「fought」把反覆爭執放在過去；原題以現在式描述目前的情況。

foils.text: The two team captains fight like cat and dog whenever they win.
foils.reason: 「whenever they win」把觸發爭吵的情況由意見不同改成勝出比賽。
